text:
maria: heads-up — I ran a focused micro-sweep for Pack+Epilogue changes across flash variants and paged-attn this morning. posting raw notes + a couple surprising regressions. :eyes:

maria: test matrix: llama-13b, seq=512/1024/2048, batch=1/2/4, kernels: flash_v1, flash_v2, paged-attn, fused-epilogue prototype. all runs pinned to same CUDA/driver.

maria: quick summary: packed QKV layout change (pack on channel dim vs pack on head dim) gives ~6-11% win on flash_v2 for long sequences, but epilogue fusion with bias+rope+dropout only helps when combined with the channel-packed layout. otherwise epilogue fusion regresses on small seqs.

ken: can you paste the perf numbers? still need to understand small-seq regression.

maria: pasted salient rows below (p50 step latency ms):
```
seq 512, batch1: flash_v2 baseline 12.8 -> channel-pack+epilogue 11.9 (-7%), head-pack+epilogue 13.2 (+3%)
seq 1024, batch1: flash_v2 baseline 22.4 -> channel-pack+epilogue 20.4 (-9%), head-pack+epilogue 23.1 (+3%)
seq 2048, batch1: flash_v2 baseline 42.1 -> channel-pack+epilogue 37.6 (-11%)
small seq 64, batch4: flash_v2 baseline 5.1 -> pack+epilogue 5.6 (+9%)
```

maria: perf counters show higher L1 store pressure on small sequences when epilogue is fused — likely extra stores for rope+bias accumulation cause spill.

sam: did you try turning off KV-cache path for the small seq runs? maybe caching changes interaction.

maria: yes — reran with KV-cache disabled: small-seq regression disappears (pack+epilogue ~5.0ms), but KV-cache enabled -> regression persists. So epilogue fusion currently increases working set when KV cache path is active.

elaine: hmm. could be our KV cache layout overlapping with epilogue temp buffers. Any flamegraphs?

maria: attached a simplified flame snapshot (textified) showing a hot store in epilogue_accumulate -> memcpy to per-head scratch. The fused path introduces a write loop across heads that wasn't present in baseline (baseline did smaller per-token writes).

ken: interesting. For long sequences the amortized cost of extra stores is dwarfed by reduced kernel launches / memory reads, hence net win. For small sequences with KV enabled the scratch touches dominate. Suggest two prongs: 1) make epilogue fusion conditional on estimated working set (seq*head_dim*bytes < threshold); 2) change pack layout to channel-first by default for fused path and keep head-pack for unfused to avoid regressing other users.

sam: +1 on heuristic gating. Also propose a microbenchmark to estimate peak scratch per request and compare against free L2/L1 budget. We can read GPU SM __free_mem? otherwise approximate from head_size*seq.

maria: prototyped a gate: if (kv_enabled && seq < 128 && batch >= 2) -> fallback to unfused epilogue. That immediately kills regression in our tests. But it's brittle — want a more principled selector in kernel chooser.

elaine: can we add a static estimator in kernel-chooser that computes worst-case ephemeral bytes and compares to a per-device configured SLO (e.g., target L1 alloc)? If estimator says high, route to paged-attn or unfused.

ken: also worth trying a lighter-weight epilogue fusion: fuse bias+gelu but postpone rope to separate small kernel that can be only enabled when seq>threshold. Rope is the heavy per-position multiply/add, could be separated to reduce working set.

maria: did a quick split: bias+gelu fused + rope in a tiny per-position kernel. That recovered ~80% of epilogue win on long seqs and removed small-seq regression entirely. downsides: two launches instead of one, but second launch is tiny and has good occupancy.

perf-bot: automated-check: microbench regression detected? NO. new heuristic gate deployed to local branch 'maria/pack-epilogue-gate'. CI bench: PASS.

sam: nice. what's next? roll to canary? we should add more permutations: batch skew, multi-request interleaving, and dedicated KV cache stress tests.

maria: agreed. action items: 1) ken to add estimator + device-config knob in kernel-chooser (owner: ken). 2) sam to extend microbench harness to include KV-heavy scenarios and multi-request interleave (owner: sam). 3) elaine to prototype the split-epilogue (bias+gelu fused, rope separate) as a fallback path and measure memory footprint (owner: elaine). 4) i'll open a PR with channel-pack as default for fused path and the gating heuristic.

ken: timeline?

maria: aiming for a small canary in next 5 working days, broader internal canary after another week pending perf bot.

elaine: i'll land split-epilogue draft by Tue and post perf snapshots.

sam: adding tests to harness now, will ping when KV-stress runs complete.

maria: thanks all. feel free to poke the branch 'maria/pack-epilogue-gate' — comments welcome. :rocket:
